approved_input.value: Visual Outcomes and Patient-Reported Symptoms after Bilateral Implantation of an Extended Depth of Focus or a Full Range of Vision Intraocular Lens

The hypothesis is that bilateral implantation of PureSee or Odyssey intraocular lenses will be associated with good distance and intermediate visual outcomes and high patient satisfaction. Near vision, spectacle use, and reports of visual disturbances may differ between the two cohorts. This observational study is intended to describe those outcomes; it is not designed to establish superiority of either lens.

The TECNIS PureSee is a non-diffractive extended depth of focus (EDOF) intraocular lens. Its design may reduce dysphotopsias and improve contrast sensitivity compared with diffractive lenses. A randomized controlled trial suggested better intermediate and near vision than a monofocal control, with similar contrast sensitivity, distance vision, and dysphotopsia profiles.1

The TECNIS Odyssey is a full range of vision intraocular lens. Current reports suggest high visual acuity and spectacle independence at distance, intermediate, and near.2,3

These reports concern the individual lens technologies. They do not establish which lens will provide better outcomes in the population proposed here. We would like to characterize vision and patient-reported symptoms in two cohorts followed using the same assessment schedule.

The objective is to describe and compare binocular visual outcomes, spectacle use, satisfaction, and visual disturbances after bilateral PureSee or bilateral Odyssey implantation through 6 months after second-eye surgery.

Lens selection will already have been made by the treating surgeon and patient as part of routine care before study enrollment. Enrollment will not determine lens selection. There will be no randomization, no masking, and no change to the planned clinical treatment. Each subject will receive the same lens model in both eyes. This study does not involve mix-and-match implantation.

All postoperative time points are measured from second-eye surgery. The interval between operations follows routine clinical care rather than a study-prescribed interval.

At screening, informed consent will be obtained, demographics and medical history recorded, and the routine-care lens selection and corresponding cohort confirmed. Each operative visit comprises cataract surgery and implantation of the planned lens model. Enrollment does not determine lens selection or change the planned clinical treatment.

items: Month 1: Measure binocular uncorrected and corrected photopic distance visual acuity and binocular uncorrected photopic intermediate visual acuity at 66 cm. Review adverse events and device deficiencies.

Month 3: Repeat binocular uncorrected and corrected photopic distance visual acuity and uncorrected photopic intermediate visual acuity at 66 cm. Measure binocular uncorrected and distance-corrected photopic near visual acuity at 40 cm, administer the AIOLIS questionnaire, and review adverse events and device deficiencies.

Month 6 (Exit): Assess binocular uncorrected and corrected photopic distance visual acuity, uncorrected and distance-corrected photopic intermediate visual acuity at 66 cm, and uncorrected and distance-corrected photopic near visual acuity at 40 cm. Obtain the distance-corrected defocus curve, administer the AIOLIS questionnaire, review adverse events and device deficiencies, and complete the exit form.

study.title: Visual Outcomes and Patient-Reported Symptoms after Bilateral Implantation of an Extended Depth of Focus or a Full Range of Vision Intraocular Lens
study.hypothesis: The hypothesis is that bilateral implantation of PureSee or Odyssey intraocular lenses will be associated with good distance and intermediate visual outcomes and high patient satisfaction. Near vision, spectacle use, and reports of visual disturbances may differ between the two cohorts. This observational study is intended to describe those outcomes; it is not designed to establish superiority of either lens.
study.background:
The TECNIS PureSee is a non-diffractive extended depth of focus (EDOF) intraocular lens. Its design may reduce dysphotopsias and improve contrast sensitivity compared with diffractive lenses. A randomized controlled trial suggested better intermediate and near vision than a monofocal control, with similar contrast sensitivity, distance vision, and dysphotopsia profiles.1

The TECNIS Odyssey is a full range of vision intraocular lens. Current reports suggest high visual acuity and spectacle independence at distance, intermediate, and near.2,3

These reports concern the individual lens technologies. They do not establish which lens will provide better outcomes in the population proposed here. We would like to characterize vision and patient-reported symptoms in two cohorts followed using the same assessment schedule.

The objective is to describe and compare binocular visual outcomes, spectacle use, satisfaction, and visual disturbances after bilateral PureSee or bilateral Odyssey implantation through 6 months after second-eye surgery.

Lens selection will already have been made by the treating surgeon and patient as part of routine care before study enrollment. Enrollment will not determine lens selection. There will be no randomization, no masking, and no change to the planned clinical treatment. Each subject will receive the same lens model in both eyes. This study does not involve mix-and-match implantation.

procedures.visit_timing: All postoperative time points are measured from surgery on the second eye. The interval between surgeries will follow routine clinical care; no fixed interval is specified by this study.
procedures.adverse_events: Adverse events and device deficiencies will be collected from consent through the final study contact. Scheduled review at Months 1, 3, and 6 is not the only time an event may be reported.
procedures.completion: A participant completes study follow-up after the 6-month assessment following second-eye surgery and completion of the exit form. Participants may withdraw voluntarily at any time.

population.study_population: Adults aged 50 years or older undergoing surgery for age-related cataracts in both eyes, with planned bilateral TECNIS PureSee or Odyssey chosen in routine care.
population.sample_justification: We estimate that 30 evaluable subjects per cohort will be sufficient for descriptive characterization of visual outcomes and patient-reported symptoms. To account for dropout or incomplete 6-month assessments, enrollment will be increased to 36 subjects per cohort, for 72 subjects total. No formal power calculation for superiority testing is proposed.
inclusion_criteria: Adults aged 50 years or older undergoing surgery for age-related cataracts in both eyes.
Planned bilateral implantation of either TECNIS PureSee or TECNIS Odyssey selected during routine clinical care before enrollment.
Willing and able to attend the scheduled study assessments.
No participation in another study during the 60 days before screening.
exclusion_criteria: Moderate-to-severe ocular disease deemed by the surgeon to increase the risk of complicated cataract surgery or prevent reliable visual-acuity testing.
Pseudoexfoliation syndrome with clinically significant zonular weakness, zonular dehiscence, prior ocular trauma affecting vision, or prior corneal refractive surgery.
Planned implantation of different lens models in the two eyes.

design.study_design: Prospective, observational, single-center, two-cohort study with no randomization and no masking. Cohorts are defined by lens selection already made in routine care: bilateral TECNIS PureSee or bilateral TECNIS Odyssey.
design.intervention_name: Bilateral TECNIS PureSee intraocular lenses or bilateral TECNIS Odyssey intraocular lenses, according to the preexisting routine-care treatment plan.
design.treatment_assignment: Lens selection will already have been made by the treating surgeon and patient as part of routine care before study enrollment. Enrollment will not determine lens selection. There will be no randomization, no masking, and no change to the planned clinical treatment. Each subject will receive the same lens model in both eyes. This study does not involve mix-and-match implantation.

paragraphs.text: At the preoperative Screening visit, obtain informed consent, record demographics and general information including medical history, and confirm the routine-care lens selection and cohort.

The Operative visits comprise one visit for each eye for cataract surgery and implantation of the planned lens model. The interval between operations follows routine clinical care. Postoperative study visits occur at Month 1, Month 3, and Month 6, with timing measured from second-eye surgery.

At Month 1, perform uncorrected photopic distance VA (binocular), corrected photopic distance VA (binocular), and uncorrected photopic intermediate VA (66 cm, binocular). Monitor for adverse events and device deficiencies.

At Month 3, repeat the binocular uncorrected and corrected photopic distance VA assessments and uncorrected photopic intermediate VA at 66 cm. Also perform uncorrected photopic near VA (40 cm, binocular) and distance-corrected photopic near VA (40 cm, binocular), administer the AIOLIS questionnaire, and monitor for adverse events and device deficiencies.

At Month 6, assess binocular uncorrected and corrected photopic distance VA, uncorrected photopic intermediate VA at 66 cm, distance-corrected photopic intermediate VA at 66 cm, and both uncorrected and distance-corrected photopic near VA at 40 cm. Obtain the distance-corrected defocus curve and administer the AIOLIS questionnaire. Monitor for adverse events and device deficiencies and complete the exit form at this visit.
Scheduled monitoring at Months 1, 3, and 6 does not limit event reporting to those visits; adverse events and device deficiencies are collected from consent through the final study contact.
